title: Sustainable Load Balancing for Wireless Networks With Renewable Energy Sources.
abstract: Future wireless networks powered by renewable energy sources and storage systems (e.g., batteries) require energy-aware mechanisms to ensure stability in critical and high-demand scenarios. These include large-scale user gatherings, especially during evening hours when solar generation is unavailable, and days with poor wind conditions that limit the effectiveness of wind-based energy harvesting. Maintaining network performance under such constraints, while preserving stored energy, remains a key challenge. This work proposes an enhanced Proactive-Reactive Load Balancing algorithm that integrates energy conditions into mobility management. By leveraging standardized mobility events, the algorithm optimizes traffic distribution and energy utilization (avoiding complete drainage of stored energy), thereby preventing service degradation. Simulations show improved energy sustainability and network performance under congestion and limited solar availability.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: ECORE: Energy-Conscious Optimized Routing for Deep Learning Models at the Edge.
abstract: Edge computing enables data processing closer to the source, significantly reducing latency, an essential requirement for real-time vision-based analytics such as object detection in surveillance and smart city environments. However, these tasks place substantial demands on resource-constrained edge devices, making the joint optimization of energy consumption and detection accuracy critical. To address this challenge, we propose ECORE , a framework that integrates multiple dynamic routing strategies, including a novel estimation-based techniques and an innovative greedy selection algorithm, to direct image processing requests to the most suitable edge device–model pair. ECORE dynamically balances energy efficiency and detection performance based on object characteristics. We evaluate our framework through extensive experiments on real-world datasets, comparing against widely used baseline techniques. The evaluation leverages established object detection models (YOLO, SSD, EfficientDet) and diverse edge platforms, including Jetson Orin Nano, Raspberry Pi 4 and 5, and TPU accelerators. Results demonstrate that our proposed context-aware routing strategies can reduce energy consumption and latency by 35% and 49%, respectively, while incurring only a 2% loss in detection accuracy compared to accuracy-centric methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Toward Massive Satellite Swarms: A Simulation Framework for Precision Formation Flying.
abstract: Future direct-to-device satellite communications may require distributed phased-array antennas formed by thousands of satellites flying in precise coordination. Evaluating control algorithms for such large formations demands simulation tools that combine high-fidelity orbital mechanics with scalable parallel execution, but existing frameworks do not satisfy both requirements. This paper presents a distributed simulation framework for large-scale satellite formation flying. The framework decomposes simulation into independent modules for orbital propagation, electromagnetic force computation, and control algorithms, connected through ROS2 publish-subscribe messaging. A snapshot-based synchronization mechanism coordinates modules at fixed intervals while orbital propagators advance with adaptive timesteps internally. We implement orbital mechanics using Orekit with perturbation models including non-spherical Earth gravity, atmospheric drag, solar radiation pressure, and third-body effects. Evaluation on formations of up to 10,000 satellites demonstrates a 7.6× speedup with 16 parallel nodes under full perturbation models, and sub-millimeter position errors below 0.4 mm RMS over 7-day two-body simulations used for numerical validation. The modular architecture allows researchers to integrate new control algorithms without modifying existing modules.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Dynamic Intelligence Placement for Real-Time Data Analytics in Smart Buildings.
abstract: Smart building applications increasingly rely on machine learning for occupancy detection, but face a critical challenge: balancing edge computing’s low latency and privacy benefits against cloud computing’s elastic scalability. This demonstration presents a practical implementation of dynamic intelligence placement using the AC3 (Agile and Cognitive Cloud-edge Continuum) framework. Our system monitors environmental sensors (temperature, humidity, CO2) deployed in a 3D-printed room model to perform real-time occupancy classification, forecasting, and anomaly detection. When edge processing latency exceeds configured thresholds due to resource constraints or increased data rates, AC3 autonomously migrates the ML application pipeline from edge to cloud infrastructure using Kubernetes-based orchestration. Attendees will observe live migration events through interactive Grafana dashboards displaying real-time sensor data, ML inference results, resource utilization metrics, and migration triggers. The demonstration showcases how cognitive continuum management, integrated with data space principles from the 6G-DALI project, enables building operators to maintain both operational efficiency and occupant privacy by defaulting to edge execution while seamlessly leveraging cloud resources when necessary.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: An Energy Efficient Convolutional SNN for EEG Analytics towards Wearable BCI Applications.
abstract: Wearable brain–computer interface (BCI) systems require real-time, energy-efficient, and privacy-preserving electroencephalogram (EEG) processing under dynamic conditions. Conventional deep learning models, despite their high accuracy, impose substantial computational demands, rendering them unsuitable for edge deployment. To address these limitations, we propose a lightweight Convolutional Spiking Neural Network (CSNN) architecture (following neuromorphic computing paradigm) that integrates temporal convolutional layers with spiking neurons for efficient representation and classification of scalp and ear EEG signals. The model supports two biologically inspired readout schemes—mean membrane potential and spike count—enabling event-driven processing with reduced complexity. Experimental evaluations on a multi-channel EEG dataset recorded under both static and movement conditions demonstrate that CSNN achieves performance comparable to EEGNet (within a 3% margin), a state-of-the-art convolutional neural network benchmark, while reducing computational cost by a factor of 40–80× and exhibiting enhanced robustness to motion artefacts. These findings establish CSNN as a promising candidate for on-device BCI inference in resource-constrained environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Context-Aware Inference in Segmentation with Block-skipping Early Exit Networks.
abstract: Deep neural networks are increasingly deployed on resource-constrained devices in IoT and pervasive computing environments, making real-time performance and heterogeneity of computing resources key challenges. Early exit networks offer a way to balance inference time and accuracy dynamically based on the input sample, but their use in dense prediction tasks like semantic segmentation has been limited and mainly focused on reducing FLOPs rather than materialized speed-ups. Inspired by input-sparse convolutions used in video processing, we propose a dynamic block-skipping approach for use in segmentation networks with early exits. This work presents a proof of concept to exploit sub-image level sparsity based on confidence thresholds to selectively bypass computations and enable faster inference. Our experiments confirm that the approach reduces runtime compared to dense convolution baselines aiding the deployment of segmentation networks in real-time, resource-constrained settings.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Strategic Collaborative Uplink for Information Freshness in Rechargeable IoT Devices.
abstract: We analyze the behavior of rechargeable Low-Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN)-enabled sensors, collaboratively performing uplink transmissions, modelled as a symmetric stochastic game in which each node independently chooses its transmission probability based on its battery state and the current age of federated information (AoFI). This formulation captures the shared-reward nature of collaborative decoding and the heterogeneous dynamics inherent in energy-harvesting systems. We derive the Markov perfect equilibrium (MPE) policy and evaluate its performance against a socially optimal benchmark that minimizes the global long-term cost. We highlight fundamental limitations of purely decentralized decision-making in collaborative LPWANs, and suggest that incentive mechanisms, lightweight coordination, or repeated-game strategies are necessary to achieve near-optimal performance.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: SignAlign: A Smartphone-Based Visual Positioning System for Enhanced Bicycle Safety.
abstract: Precise positioning of cyclists is critical for road safety applications, yet there is no pervasive approach for it. We present SignAlign, a pervasive system that enables sub-meter positioning using only a smartphone, which many road users already carry. SignAlign uses a smartphone camera to detect road signs and estimates the distance to them. These signs act as reference points to determine a cyclist’s global position by matching them to known map data, such as a city’s digital twin. We evaluate SignAlign through real-world experiments in different urban environments. Results show that our approach achieves a median positioning accuracy of 0.64m. We show that in road safety applications (i.e., cooperative collision avoidance systems), SignAlign can reduce the probability of missing a collision from 0.61 to 0.005, compared to smartphone GNSS positioning. We demonstrate the real-life feasibility of SignAlign by showing that it maintains robust results even during nighttime. Furthermore, our proposed system can already cover large areas of cities around the world without requiring extra infrastructure. We show that SignAlign can operate on battery-constrained hardware, such as smartphones, in real time. By using only a smartphone, SignAlign offers a scalable, low-cost solution for enhancing pervasive road safety in urban mobility.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: "Thoughtful Coordination": LLM Reasoning for Anomaly Detection in Complex Activity Sensing.
abstract: Complex human activities, such as cooking, exhibit characteristic coordination patterns across multiple body parts, and unexpected events often disrupt this coordination. In this work, we investigate whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with visual prompting can directly detect such anomalies from IMU accelerometer plots, without requiring activity labels or anomalous examples. We first conduct a pilot study on a kitchen activity dataset to show that MLLMs can reliably infer the body location of an IMU sensor from its plotted signal, indicating that plot-based representations retain limb-specific motion structure. Building on this, we evaluate anomaly detection across multiple prompt designs and state-of-the-art MLLMs. Prompts that explicitly emphasize body-position-based coordination achieve an average anomaly detection accuracy of ≈79%, outperforming coordination-agnostic baselines. These results suggest that body-position-aware prompting (BPP) enables MLLMs to reason about inter-limb synchronization, improving the recognition of abnormal behavior during activities of daily living (ADLs).
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Optimization Potential for Adapting Symbolic Regression Models Applied to Energy Flow Control.
abstract: In recent publications, symbolic regression models developed using genetic programming have been introduced for the optimization of the energy flows in households with photovoltaic (PV) systems that include a battery. These models pursue the objective of minimizing the energy costs of a household.The globally optimal solution for energy flow control is determined in this paper using dynamic programming, in order to provide a performance assessment of the resulting energy costs when the symbolic regression model is applied.In the performance assessment, the resulting energy costs after simulation using energy tariffs and power measurements for two different households are compared. The results show that the symbolic regression models achieve cost values close to the globally optimal solution for the data they have been trained with. For different time spans, the remaining optimization potential takes values of up to approximately ten percent.Moreover, the symbolic regression models have been applied to energy flow control of a new system, for which the original model had not been trained. The optimization potential on this new system makes up more than thirty percent.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Integrating Learnable Spatial Embeddings into Transformers for Traffic Flow Forecasting.
abstract: Traffic flow forecasting is a crucial component of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), contributing to more efficient road management and congestion mitigation. While recent advancements in deep learning, particularly Transformer based time series models, have shown strong capabilities in capturing temporal dependencies, they often overlook the spatial correlations inherent in traffic networks. In this study, we introduce a Transformer architecture enhanced with learnable spatial embeddings that enrich token-level representations and enable the model to capture underlying road traffic structures. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms existing baselines on both publicly available benchmark datasets and a real-world traffic dataset collected from the metropolitan city of Istanbul, Turkey.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: ViT-Curated Transfer Learning for Resource-Constrained UAV Detection.
abstract: In many real-world applications, particularly those involving critical infrastructure monitoring and inspection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), there is often a significant lack of high-quality, domain-specific datasets. This scarcity of quality training data presents substantial challenges for deploying effective object detection models in resource-constrained environments. To address these limitations, this paper presents a novel Vision Transformer (ViT)-based data curation approach for enhanced transfer learning efficiency in object detection. Our methodology leverages ViT embeddings and cosine similarity matching to intelligently select training samples that maximize domain alignment and model performance. The approach focuses on scenarios where acquiring sufficient quality datasets is challenging, promoting techniques that maximize the utility of limited training data through strategic data selection rather than extensive data collection. We demonstrate that our ViT-based similarity matching can achieve a 30% reduction in training data requirements while maintaining performance within 3% of full-dataset training. To complement this data curation strategy, we also explore strategic layer freezing in YOLO architectures to preserve pre-trained knowledge during transfer learning. Experiments conducted on four diverse datasets relevant to infrastructure inspection validate the effectiveness of our data curation approach, showing that intelligent data selection provides a practical solution for deploying object detection models in data-scarce, resource-constrained environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Leveraging Open Static and Real-Time Data for Submarine Cable Analysis and Prediction.
abstract: Submarine fiber-optic cables form the backbone of global Internet connectivity, yet monitoring their exposure to environmental and operational risks remains challenging due to fragmented and heterogeneous data sources. This work-in-progress explores how open data, ranging from slowly updated infrastructure datasets to high-frequency feeds on earthquakes, hurricanes, and public news, can be leveraged to build a near-real-time monitoring framework for submarine cable systems. Our approach distinguishes between static open datasets, which describe the stable geographical structure of the cable network, and dynamic open datasets, which model spatio-temporal events interacting with that structure. We present a framework for integrating these sources into a unified architecture supporting continuous ingestion, temporal storage, event generation, and preliminary situational awareness. This paper reports early steps toward data harmonization and event modeling and outlines the challenges of orchestrating open data streams with differing semantics, formats, and temporal granularities. The long-term goal is to transform open data into a pervasive sensing fabric enabling real-time risk detection and prediction for critical submarine communication infrastructure.

title: Investigating Demographic Bias in Eye-Tracking-based Machine Learning Models for Affective Computing.
abstract: Eye-tracking is a central technology in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) for capturing behavioral and emotional aspects of user-product interactions. Studies have shown that distinct eye movement patterns can reveal insights into affective computing, such as user perceptions of usability and user experience (UX). Machine learning models are increasingly applied to analyze these interactions, but their generalizability remains largely unexplored, particularly with respect to different user groups and demographics. This is especially relevant in eye-tracking research, where datasets primarily consist of young students who are often easiest to recruit. This study investigates how factors such as age and education influence the generalizability of affective machine learning models trained on eye movement data. Two machine learning models — a Support Vector Machine and a Multi-Layer Perceptron — were trained on multiple sub-datasets derived from an eye-tracking study involving 121 participants who interacted with and rated six websites based on perceived usability and UX. The results indicate that model predictions were more reliable for participants aged 25 and older, yielding medium to large Cohen’s d effect sizes of 0.677 compared to a randomly sampled dataset of equal size, and 0.783 when compared against the full dataset. In contrast, different education levels showed no significant influence, with effect sizes ranging between 0.115 and 0.160.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Verbeth: Secure Messaging over the Blockchain Event Logs.
abstract: This work explores whether the public log layer of an EVM compatible ledger can act as a minimal and globally reachable transport for encrypted communication. We present Verbeth, a proof of concept protocol that uses ordinary wallet keys and per message forward secrecy to send ciphertext directly through transaction logs. The design requires no auxiliary servers and offers strong censorship resistance and guaranteed final delivery, while revealing the economic and cryptographic limits of on chain messaging. We also compare it with established messaging protocols to clarify where its guarantees align and where they diverge. Looking ahead, the protocol can absorb hybrid or post quantum designs that remove harvest now decrypt later concerns and place its security profile on par with other messengers.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: SolarTrack: Exploring the Continuous Tracking Capabilities of Wearable Solar Harvesters.
abstract: Continuous tracking is often thought to require specialised, actively powered sensors. Yet energy harvesters already embedded in commercial devices, such as Garmin solar-powered smartwatches, generate energy signals that inherently carry continuous variations linked to user motion and environment. Prior studies have shown that these signals are sufficient for classification tasks such as human activity and gesture recognition by exploiting class-distinguishing cues. However, whether they can support continuous trajectory tracking has remained an open question-until now.In this paper, we present the first fundamental study of continuous hand trajectory tracking with wearable solar harvesters. Through a novel radiometric model, we analytically link photovoltaic (PV) power to the solar cell’s geometric configuration, exposing both the promise of energy signals for tracking and their core limitations: the positional ambiguities and distortions that arise when power is used directly for positioning. To resolve this ambiguity, we propose SolarTrack, a framework that embeds a radiometric model as a physical backbone within a sequence-learning pipeline, enforcing cycle consistency between data-driven predictions and physical feasibility. This yields the first standalone solar-based tracker capable of estimating continuous hand motion directly from harvested energy signals.To validate this, we built a wearable prototype with a solar panel and IMU and collected the first dataset pairing motion-capture ground truth with harvested energy from 15 participants (700k samples). Results show that solar signals alone achieve subdecimeter tracking accuracy, outperforming purely data-driven baselines and only 1.6 cm worse compared to the IMU tracker despite having access to only 1D power signal. Furthermore, when fused with IMU, it further boosts IMU performance by 13%.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Multimodal Data Integration for Intelligent Vehicular Safety in Smart Cities.
abstract: This paper presents a pervasive computing frame-work for intelligent vehicular safety that integrates vision sensing, satellite infrastructure features, and crowdsourced geospatial data in an operational smart city testbed. A unified 100 m grid representation combines Sentinel 2 RGB imagery, Open-StreetMap infrastructure annotations, and privacy-preserving video analytics from roadside cameras. Each grid cell is characterized by geometric indicators (road width, intersection density, building density) and semantic attributes (pedestrian crossings, traffic signals), together with safety events including speed violations, pedestrian crossing issues, congestion levels, and historical accidents. Correlation analysis reveals strong associations between infrastructure and safety outcomes (e.g., intersection density vs. congestion: r = 0.911), highlighting the complementary value of satellite and volunteered geographic information. On this multimodal feature space, machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, SVR) outperform regularized linear baselines for predicting safety indicators, and spatial k-fold cross-validation confirms acceptable generalization to unseen areas. The proposed architecture thus provides interpretable, infrastructure-aware risk maps that can inform V2X communications, path planning, and traffic management, while operating under strict privacy constraints. The work establishes a practical foundation for future, more advanced fusion modules that learn joint representations from Sentinel 2 imagery, OSM semantics, and camera-derived events for road safety prediction.

title: Backrunning MEV on Ethereum: A Multi-Layer Framework for Measurement and Detection.
abstract: Backrunning is one of the most prevalent forms of Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) on Ethereum, yet its underlying dynamics across the mempool, block production, and peer-to-peer layers remain insufficiently understood. This paper presents a multi-layer measurement and detection framework that simultaneously captures mempool snapshots, block-level execution data, and network-layer peer information from a live Ethereum mainnet full node. Using datasets ranging from 5 to 4,500 consecutive blocks, we analyze how transaction arrival times, propagation characteristics, and local network visibility influence opportunities for backrunning MEV. Our empirical results reveal that DEX swap arrival-time distributions are highly consistent across experiments, with 80% to 90% of swaps entering the mempool within 15s of inclusion. Backrunning emerges as a persistent behavior, consistently affecting 5% to 6% of DEX swaps once the observation window exceeds 300 blocks. Timing analysis further shows that victim and backrun transactions frequently coexist in the mempool for multiple seconds, indicating that successful MEV strategies rely on multi-second positioning and fee-based ordering rather than ultra-low-latency reaction. Network-layer measurements confirm stable peer connectivity, ensuring reliable mempool visibility throughout the experiments. These results show that backrunning relies on multi second mempool coexistence and fee-based ordering rather than sub-second network latency, which block traces alone cannot capture. Correlating mempool visibility, block ordering, and peer stability on live Ethereum mainnet, we provide a reproducible baseline for measuring MEV behavior under the current block building workflow.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Enhancing ECG Classification Robustness with Lightweight Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Filters.
abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring via wearable devices is vital for early cardiovascular disease detection. However, deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained microcontrollers faces reliability challenges, particularly from Out-of-Distribution (OOD) pathologies and noise. Standard classifiers often yield high-confidence errors on such data. Existing OOD detection methods either neglect computational constraints or address noise and unseen classes separately. This paper investigates Unsupervised Anomaly Detection (UAD) as a lightweight, upstream filtering mechanism. We perform a Neural Architecture Search (NAS) on six UAD approaches, including Deep Support Vector Data Description (Deep SVDD), input reconstruction with (Variational-)Autoencoders (AE/VAE), Masked Anomaly Detection (MAD), Normalizing Flows (NFs) and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) under strict hardware constraints (<=512k parameters), suitable for microcontrollers. Evaluating on the PTB-XL and BUT QDB datasets, we demonstrate that a NAS-optimized Deep SVDD offers the superior Pareto efficiency between detection performance and model size. In a simulated deployment, this lightweight filter improves the accuracy of a diagnostic classifier by up to 21.0 percentage points, demonstrating that optimized UAD filters can safeguard ECG analysis on wearables.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: D-SYNC: Enhancing Vehicle Localization with Dashcam-Satellite Image Synchronization.
abstract: This paper introduces D-SYNC, a cutting-edge framework for enhancing the security and reliability of vehicle localization systems. D-SYNC offers an innovative solution to utilize dashcam footage for vehicle localization in the scenario of the primary localization system, GPS, under security attacks or simply failing to work. D-SYNC synchronizes the visual data from dashcam recordings with geotagged satellite imagery, achieving reliable vehicle positioning and trajectory mapping without precise dashcam-to-satellite alignment. D-SYNC introduces novel designs to address critical challenges, such as the limited field of vision in dashcam videos during real-world driving and how to correlate the significantly distinct spatial and temporal patterns between dashcam sequences and satellite images. Moreover, a novel geo-assisted loss function is introduced in D-SYNC that further elevates the performance of the localization process. D-SYNC surpasses existing methods and significantly increases vehicle localization accuracy. It achieves a 91% top-1 retrieval accuracy in urban environments and a 34% improvement in sub-10 meter localization error compared to benchmarks, relying solely on dashcam and satellite imagery.

title: Dynamic Cooperative Energy and Coverage Management for V2G-Enhanced RAN Resilience.
abstract: he resilience of cellular communication is paramount, given how widely its services are used. However, it also depends on the resilience of the power grid, which is increasingly threatened by extreme weather events and the growing reliance on distributed, intermittent energy sources. Current base station backup systems, typically limited to 2-6 hours of autonomy, operate in isolation and fail to leverage spatial redundancy. This paper proposes the Multi-Site Resiliency Cooperative (MSRC) framework, a unified control strategy that transforms independent sites into a collaborative energy cluster. We formulate a two-stage mixed-integer optimization problem that jointly manages radio coverage adaptation switching sites between helping, assisted, and deep-sleep modes and dynamic Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) energy injection. By proactively reshaping cell boundaries and traffic loads based on real-time battery states, MSRC maximizes network survival while prioritizing critical service classes. Extensive simulations on a 19-site urban network demonstrate that the proposed framework extends survival time by 96% and maintains 94% service continuity compared to conventional baselines. Crucially, MSRC requires no physical in- frastructure upgrades, offering operators a deployable, software- defined solution for outage-resilient green communications.

title: Tiny-ish ML for Big Impact: How to Utilise EdgeAI in Software-Defined Vehicles.
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) algorithms are commonly used in vehicles as part of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in time and safety-critical systems. Thus, maximising the speed of the algorithm and minimising latency while preserving the accuracy of the ML models is vitally important. At the same time, vehicles as edge devices are constrained environments with limited processing capabilities, power, and internet connectivity. However, algorithms for ADAS require a significant amount of processing power, and pure tinyML algorithms might become insufficient. Hence, there is a need to implement vehicular Edge AI. This paper outlines a research plan for evaluating different ML/AI distribution solutions in the vehicular environment, with a practical use case of object detection from FLIR ADK 2.0 thermal camera data on NVIDIA’s constrained edge device, the Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit. Additionally, the more demanding task of sensor fusion with lidar data is attempted. As a result, the latency and accuracy of different solutions will be evaluated within real-world use cases.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: HyperEcho: Structured Higher Order Representation for Automotive Radar Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: Automotive radar is attractive for perception in adverse weather and lighting conditions, but semantic segmentation on radar maps is still difficult. Objects in radar heatmaps are sparse and noisy, appearing as extended blobs or streaks rather than neat contours. Most existing CNN and transformer backbones treat these maps like ordinary images and rely on local filters or pairwise attention, which makes it hard to capture the larger echo patterns that define objects. We propose HyperEcho, a backbone that is tailored to radar feature maps. Instead of reasoning only over individual pixels, HyperEcho builds a simple hypergraph on top of the feature map: it learns a few groups of positions along the range and angle/Doppler axes that each capture an echo pattern, runs a lightweight attention mechanism over these groups, and then propagates the result back to the underlying pixels. This axial hypergraph backbone can be used on its own or combined with a lightweight contrastive loss that encourages consistent features across radar views. On the CARRADA benchmark, HyperEcho consistently improves semantic segmentation over strong CNN and transformer baselines. Our best variant sets a new state of the art on both Range–Doppler and Range–Angle segmentation, achieving 62.4% mIoU on RD and 45.1% mIoU on RA, showing that explicitly modelling higher-order echo structure is beneficial for radar scene understanding.

title: CompulsEar: Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors Detection Using Earable-based Inertial Sensing.
abstract: Body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) such as nail biting, hair pulling, beard pulling, and face itching are common compulsive habits, affecting approximately 20-30% of the population and often going unnoticed until they cause visible physical and psychological harm. Existing monitoring approaches typically rely on self-report, clinician observation, or camera-based systems, which are intrusive, environment-constrained, or difficult to scale in everyday settings. To address this challenge, we propose CompulsEar, an earable-based framework that employs Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) signals from commercially available earables to detect BFRB episodes in situ. Our system captures characteristic motion patterns associated with four BFRB types (nail biting, beard pulling, hair pulling, and face itching). We conducted a user study with 12 diverse participants, highlighting the potential of earable-based sensing as a non-intrusive and scalable foundation for continuous BFRB monitoring and just-in-time intervention.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Beyond the Beaten Path: Using Gamification to Expand Urban Crowdsensing Coverage.
abstract: Uneven data coverage is a challenge in location-based crowd sensing. This paper investigates whether gamification can improve data coverage by motivating users to explore less frequently visited areas. Building on concepts of crowd sensing and gamification in the context of promoting changes in human mobility behavior, an online survey was developed. In the ongoing survey (n = 346), participants are presented with route-selection scenarios that vary in travel context and route length. Preliminary insights indicate that user behavior is influenced by a combination of contextual and perceptual factors, while basic gamification components may offer limited leverage for directing exploration. The findings suggest that more adaptive and personalized incentive strategies are needed to achieve a balanced and comprehensive coverage of urban environments in mobility data collection.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Privacy-Preserving Skeleton-Based Analysis of Visitor Behavior in Museums.
abstract: This study uses depth-sensor technology to characterize visitors’ spatial and social behavior, including engagement in museum environments. Museums are complex spaces that serve as centers of learning and social interaction, attracting diverse populations. Traditional methods of studying visitor interaction with exhibits are often intrusive and costly, requiring specially trained personnel to analyze data. To address these challenges, we propose a system to automatically analyze skeleton data collected from an on-site deployed solution using a set of Kinect v2 sensors across exhibition spaces at the Musikinstrumenten-Museum in Berlin. The system captures detailed information on visitor-exhibition interaction through body joints as skeleton data, providing insights into how designated areas and object placement influence engagement. By using raw skeleton data to derive high-level features, such as dwell time, proximity, pointing gestures, and qualitative observations of group dynamics, we compute spatial and behavioral metrics of visitors while avoiding the storage of identifiable audio or video data and aiming to preserve visitor privacy. The depth camera system enables tracking and displaying visitor interactions, offering a non-intrusive, interactive way to measure attention and engagement. With this study, we demonstrate the feasibility of skeleton-based sensing for automated unobtrusive assessment of human behavior indoors.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Keynote: LLMs and Physical Simulations for Sensor Based Context Recognition in Open Ended Settings.
abstract: Keynote AbstractGenerative AI is attracting rapidly growing interest in sensor-based human activity and context recognition. Yet, its impact in this domain remains far less transformative than in computer vision, where contemporary foundation models can reliably produce accurate descriptions for a wide range of arbitrary visual scenes. The prospect of an analogous capability for arbitrary "sensor scenes" is highly compelling, but, despite an expanding body of research and encouraging early results, it is still far from being realized in practice.This talk will analyze the fundamental reasons behind the discrepancy between the remarkable progress in vision-centric generative AI and the comparatively modest gains observed in sensor-based context and activity recognition, including issues of the variability of the input space, data heterogeneity, limited large-scale labeled corpora, weak semantic grounding of sensor signals, and challenges in cross-modal generalization. Building on this analysis, the talk will outline how a combination of appropriately adapted multimodal generative models tightly coupled with physics-informed simulation and sensor-aware representation learning can solve those problems enabling more robust, generalizable, and scalable activity and context recognition systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: GAP: A Browser-Only Toolkit for Evaluating Multimodal RAG.
abstract: We present GAP, an open-source, zero-install, browser-only toolkit that automatically evaluates Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) systems on real engineering formula reasoning. Users simply upload structured JSON predictions produced by any MRAG pipeline; GAP instantly computes three orthogonal metrics against 200 expert-crafted questions derived from 10 authoritative technical documents (standards, datasheets, and manuals): (1) Ground Formula: symbolic correctness of extracted LaTeX formulas, (2) Answer Accuracy: numerical or algebraic correctness of the final solution, (3) Provenance Accuracy: faithfulness of cited document and page. Evaluation of eight frontier multimodal MLLMs reveals a universal pathology: provenance accuracy exceeds 98%, yet formula grounding and answer accuracy collapse below 7%. Current MRAG systems reliably locate the correct page but almost always hallucinate or mangle the underlying mathematics. Running entirely client-side, GAP provides the first standardized, reproducible, and instantly accessible way to quantify symbolic reliability in quantitative engineering tasks. The code and online demo of the GAP MRAG evaluation toolkit can be found here.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: The Role of Transformers and Positional Encoding in Detecting Cyclic Patterns from Wearables Data.
abstract: Human behavior follows hidden biological rhythms that shape mental and physical health. Using mobile and wearable data, we compare classic rhythm-based features with transformer models that learn temporal structure through Positional Encoding. We find that transformers often perform better, especially on longer and more regular data, but are less interpretable, highlighting a trade-off between accuracy and insight.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: On-Device AI for Voice-Driven Multi-Parameter Health-Risk Monitoring.
abstract: The proliferation of digital health systems has generated vast amounts of sensitive patient data, unlocking opportunities for enhanced disease prediction, diagnosis, and treatment via advanced analytics. However, preventive telemedicine demands continuous monitoring for proactive, personalized care, where traditional methods often fail to detect rapid physiological changes, particularly in low-connectivity or remote environments. This gap poses significant risks for patients with chronic or post-surgical conditions, necessitating robust, offline-capable solutions.Building on our prior voice-driven mobile health application, this paper integrates an on-device AI model to enable real-time, multi-parameter health-risk prediction on smartphones. A lightweight Deep Neural Network (DNN), deployed via Tensor-Flow Lite, executes locally to generate personalized risk scores, triggering immediate voice alerts and on-screen warnings upon detecting abnormal patterns. In addition, the platform supports text-or voice-based entry of six vital signs and securely stores all measurements and predictions for clinical review through a cloud backend. By combining natural voice interaction, offline reliability, wearable integration, and efficient on-device inference, this scalable and privacy-preserving solution enables continuous monitoring and early anomaly detection in both urban and rural areas.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Keynote: Trends in Space Technologies for Expanding the Potential of Terrestrial Pervasive Computing.
abstract: Space development and utilization have changed significantly over the past decade, and this transformation is expected to continue. Whereas spacecraft were traditionally designed as expensive stand alone systems operated in limited numbers, reductions in launch cost, such as those achieved by SpaceX Falcon 9 and Starship, together with the increasing use of commercial technologies, have enabled the rapid deployment of large scale small satellite constellations, exemplified by Starlink. These trends are often referred to as NewSpace, yet their background and implications are not widely understood outside the space community. This keynote first reviews how space systems are evolving from isolated platforms to systems that are continuously integrated with terrestrial information and communication technologies. Recent advances such as low Earth orbit satellite constellations, the use of commercial off the shelf technology in orbit, inter satellite links, and Non Terrestrial Networks that integrate satellite communications with terrestrial cellular networks are introduced in a manner accessible to audiences without prior expertise in space systems. The talk then highlights how these advances expand the capabilities of terrestrial pervasive computing, in which computation, communication, and sensing operate seamlessly without user awareness, as required by applications such as autonomous driving, the Internet of Things, and Cyber Physical Systems. Examples include services that become possible only when previously unconnected regions are integrated into information and communication technology systems, as well as the utilization of wide area and high frequency remote sensing data from space. Finally, the keynote introduces the speaker’s work on formation flying and satellite clustering as new spacecraft operation paradigms, in which multiple spacecraft operate cooperatively as an invisible extension of terrestrial information and communication technology infrastructure.

title: Quantification Of Correctness Of Squat From Real-Time 3D Posture Evaluation.
abstract: Squat is one of the most widely-adopted exercises for strengthening the lower body, especially quadriceps and ham-strings. If not performed correctly, especially as a part of rehabilitation while recovering from a lower body injury, it can cause lower back pain, severe knee injuries, and muscle imbalance. We present a fully automated, 3D posture monitoring and assessment system which works in real-time using Google’s Mediapipe pose land marking, powered with our customized scoring based on the type of squat prescribed by a physiotherapist. Our assessment model calculates clinically relevant parameters like squat depth, squat bias, stance width etc. as defined in literature for a certain prescribed variant of squat, which itself can be recorded as a reference profile in the system by the physiotherapist extracted from sample repetitions performed by them personalized for their patient. A score report is generated for a squat session, quantifying the quality of squat being performed by the patient compared against the prescribed variant. The comparison score is generated on-device using sigmoid-based metric customized for every parameter, without requiring heavy computations or prior dataset like in a DL-based assessment model. The pipeline is robust to environmental and demographic factors. In this demonstration, we aim to show the capability of real-time scoring using multiple reference profiles for different squat variants at the venue. This is a step forward towards a safer exercising and reliable remote rehabilitation monitoring.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: BRAIN: Blockchain-Based Reputation Architecture for Interest-flooding Neutralization in NDNs.
abstract: Named Data Networking (NDN) can face critical security vulnerabilities from Interest Flooding Attacks (IFA), where malicious nodes exhaust router resources through excessive requests for nonexistent content. The current existing NDN defense mechanisms lack persistent cross-session accountability, allowing attackers to rejoin networks with clean reputations after disconnection. Meanwhile, blockchain technology promises distributed trust management without centralized authorities, yet traditional blockchain architectures impose prohibitive latency and computational overhead for real-time network security applications. This paper presents a novel Blockchain-based Reputation Architecture and Information Networking (BRAIN) that demonstrates the feasibility of distributed ledger technology (DLT) for network forwarding security. BRAIN utilizes a microchain design with reputation-weighted consensus, localized trust domains, and constant-time per-packet enforcement that maintains accountability across network sessions while achieving sub-second block finality. Our proof-of-concept BRIAN implementation integrates lightweight blockchain operations with NDN’s forwarding plane through reputation-based admission control and graduated enforcement policies. Initial experimental validation demonstrates that BRAIN achieves 97% detection accuracy against coordinated flooding attacks while reducing router resource exhaustion by 93%, with an average latency of 10 milliseconds, representing a 75% improvement over traditional blockchain-enabled network architectures. These preliminary results indicate that blockchain-based reputation management can operate at network-forwarding speeds, opening the possibility of distributed trust mechanisms in latency-sensitive pervasive computing environments.

title: Personal Data Ecosystems in Decentralised Clinical Trials.
abstract: The organisation-centric model of data management arguably constrains portability, transparency, and individual agency, limitations that are particularly acute in health research. This paper explores Personal Data Ecosystems (PDEs) as an alternative, specifically within the context of participant discovery for decentralised clinical trials. Building on the ESPRESSO framework for Efficient Search over Personal Repositories – Secure and Sovereign, we explore a decentralised search mechanism that employs Personal Online Datastores (PODs) to facilitate data aggregation and selective sharing, thereby enforcing differential visibility and fine-grained access control. We discuss the performance of this system in the context of privacy-preserving keyword queries across metropolitan-scale cohorts, aiming to merge authoritative centralised records with POD-based streams derived from user-provided wearable and smartphone technologies, which offer unique insights into symptoms and individual performance. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through a proof-of-concept implementation on HAT/Dataswyft, complementing prior investigations on Solid, and discuss practical challenges such as API governance and structured data indexing. Finally, we outline how PDEs and compute-to-data paradigms may enable self-sovereign AI, enabling federated learning and inference sovereignty. Our findings suggest a trajectory toward secure, participatory, and interoperable health data infrastructures.

title: Beyond Data Scarcity: A Physics-Integrated Landslide Prediction for Urban Disaster Resilience.
abstract: Global climate change has increased the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events, causing landslides even in regions with little or no historical disaster records. Accurately predicting such events in urban environments requires integrating heterogeneous environmental data within a system-level co-design framework. However, two key challenges hinder reliable prediction: (i) limited observability due to scarce disaster records and the difficulty of measuring essential physical variables such as subsurface hydrology, and (ii) strong regional heterogeneity, where disaster data exhibit inherently non-IID characteristics across regions. Traditional physics-based models often rely on simplified assumptions because observable variables are limited, whereas deep learning models tend to overfit under scarce and imbalanced data. To address these issues, this study proposes a physics-integrated deep learning system that combines a three-layer tank model as a physics-based model with a data-driven deep learning model. The physics-based outputs are incorporated both as input features and through a skip-connection that adaptively controls their contribution under abnormal rainfall conditions. In addition, Stochastic Feature Augmentation is employed to improve robustness against regional data distribution shifts. Experiments conducted across 19 regions in Japan demonstrate that the proposed system achieves improved generalization and superior PR-AUC in even unseen regions compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: AcoustiMeal: Estimating Meal Duration using Audio Tagging on Smartphones.
abstract: Eating behaviour plays a vital role in the gradual development of chronic diseases such as heart disease, obesity, etc. Estimating meal duration is an integral part of measuring eating behaviour. Audio modality offers a wealth of information that can be leveraged to estimate meal durations and other meal-time activities, providing health psychology researchers with deeper insights. In this demonstration paper, we introduce an Android application, AcoustiMeal, that utilises a pre-trained audio tagging model, E-PANN, to estimate meal time and duration in a privacy-preserving and unobtrusive manner.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Tactile Urbanism Demo: A Nature-Themed Sensor-Box Game for Smart Playful Public Spaces.
abstract: This demo presents Tactile Urbanism, a sensor-box platform that turns public spaces into playful, nature-themed smart environments. The system consists of multiple interactive boxes with embedded processing, light, sound, and tactile input, orchestrated by a central Game-Master running a finite state machine that controls the overall game flow. Building on a previous outdoor deployment in a public square, we adapt the installation for an indoor pervasive computing demo using custom stands for accessibility, battery powered operation, and a layout that can be dispersed across the demo area. Conference attendees will be able to play a light sequence game while a live dashboard reveals internal system state and interaction traces. The demo highlights how exploration, collaboration, and failure manifest in the system and positions the platform as a reusable testbed for studying interaction and orchestration in smart public spaces. We invite feedback on legibility, inclusiveness, and perceived robustness.

title: Edge-Assisted Federated Learning for Real-Time Stress Detection in Wearable IoMT Systems.
abstract: Wearables increasingly enable monitoring of bio-indicators, such as stress levels, but deploying machine learning systems across heterogeneous sensors remains challenging due to privacy constraints and substantial variability in signal quality. In this paper, we investigate federated learning for stress detection using both ECG and PPG-derived features. We introduce a lightweight, VAE-based generative repair mechanism to reconstruct anomalous data windows to improve data quality in a privacy-preserving fashion. Using the WESAD dataset, we compare baseline and generatively repaired pipelines across modalities and show that FL can achieve competitive accuracy, though benefits from reconstruction remain modest. Rather than targeting immediate performance gains, this study a broader research agenda for integrating generative models with FL to build more robust, quality-aware biosensing systems capable of operation across diverse real-world wearable datasets.

title: Multi-Source Context Integration for Forecasting Urban Mobility Flows.
abstract: Deep learning models for traffic forecasting are constrained by limitations inherent in the input data. This paper investigates the integration of multi-source contextual data to overcome this limitation. We propose a two-fold contribution: a flexible framework to benchmark diverse feature extraction and fusion strategies integrated within a state-of-the-art Attention-Transformer based model, and a Spatio-Temporal Disaggregated Assessment methodology. The latter deconstructs model performance across temporal scales and specific event types to isolate the marginal value of contextual information, which is often masked by global aggregate metrics. Extensive experiments on real-world subway and micromobility datasets in Lyon, France, demonstrate that effective data integration yields significant accuracy gains-up to 7.5%-in specific, operationally critical scenarios such as adverse weather conditions or peak commute hours, despite limited improvements in global error rates.

title: Keynote - Beyond Accuracy: The Good, the Bad, and the Unknown in Sensor-Based Human Behavior Modeling.
abstract: Over twenty years, ubiquitous computing research has transformed everyday environments into rich sources of behavioral insight. Today, data-driven models built on mobile, wearable, and physiological sensors can infer activities, routines, affect, and even identity – often beyond what system designers intended. This keynote revisits the field’s evolution through the lens of "the good, the bad, and the unknown": the good –powerful models enabling health, education, and well-being applications; the bad – fragility, bias, and opaque inference pipelines; and the unknown – emergent, unintended capabilities in AI-driven sensing systems. I will outline open research directions for a future where pervasive systems remain trustworthy, meaningful, and aligned with human values.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Attention Feature Fusion with Cluster Contrastive Learning for Snoring and Breath-Holding Detection Using Seismic Sensing.
abstract: Snoring and breath-stopping are key symptoms of sleep apnea. Most existing studies primarily focus on wearable devices or smartphone-based systems. Wearable devices can be uncomfortable, while smartphone-based systems often require specific angles, distances, or positions, making them sensitive to environmental changes. This paper proposes a contactless and engagement-free system for snoring and breath-stopping detection using a seismic sensor. Distinguishing between snoring, breath-stopping, and normal breathing from raw data alone is challenging. Snoring features typically reside in a higher frequency range than breath-stopping and normal breathing, with breath-stopping features appearing in a lower frequency range. Calculating the differential and integral of raw data can enhance features in low and high frequencies, respectively. We introduce AFFCL, an attention feature fusion and contrastive learning framework to leverage information from differential and integral signals. AFFCL generates both shared and exclusive features from the differential and integral signals and employs an attention mechanism for feature fusion. Additionally, cluster-level supervised contrastive learning in AFFCL further enhances system performance. Our system has been performed 5-fold cross-validation on 44 people, which achieves an average accuracy of 93.40% and an F1 score of 92.42%. The accuracy for detecting breath-stopping, snoring, and normal breathing are 89.54%, 94.60%, and 96.06%, respectively. Evaluation results demonstrate that our system effectively identifies breath-stopping and snoring.

title: Authenticity and Confidentiality in Flow-Based Closed-Loop Molecular Communication Systems.
abstract: The Internet of Bio-Nano Things envisions networks of nanoscale devices deployed within the human body. In this wave-denied environment, communication faces novel challenges, leading to the emergence of molecular communication as a bio-compatible and energy-efficient solution for exchanging information. Securing this novel communication paradigm is a critical challenge. Existing security schemes are designed for diffusion-based models, which are not suited for the human cardiovascular system where signal propagation is mainly affected by flow-based, closed-loop dynamics. To address this, we introduce a flow-based closed-loop system model for molecular communication. Specifically, we analyze the application of channel impulse response-based authentication in this new environment, identify challenges in achieving confidentiality, and propose a novel key-exchange scheme that leverages the unique properties of the model.

title: Hierarchical Routing for Ultra-High-Speed Communication in Pico-Satellite Formations.
abstract: In realizing direct-to-device non-terrestrial networks (D2D-NTN), a formation-flying swarm of LEO satellites can function as a very large virtual phased-array antenna. To support such an operation, the satellite swarm requires a network capable of distributing beamforming parameters (e.g., 15 bytes per satellite) to more than 10,000 satellites with millisecond-scale end-to-end latency. This paper designs a two-tier hierarchical subgroup routing (HSR) architecture consisting of 85 anchor satellites and over 10,000 child satellites. Each anchor covers up to 139 child satellites located in its Voronoi region, which is further divided into subgroups of at most 70 satellites. In the proposed architecture, beamforming parameters are first sent to each anchor satellite (139 × 15 bytes ≈ 2,100 bytes). Each anchor then forwards the parameters to the satellites in its subgroups using a single multi-hop path constructed for each subgroup. The required update rate for beamforming parameters is approximately 100 Hz. To evaluate whether the proposed architecture can meet this requirement, we built a testbed using commercial mmWave communication devices and Raspberry Pi boards. We emulated (1) the throughput needed to deliver beamforming parameters to 85 anchors (required: 143 Mb/s), and (2) the latency required for each anchor to transmit parameters to up to 70 satellites in its subgroup over an 84-hop path (required: 1–10 ms). As a result, we achieved more than 900 Mb/s for (1), while the measured latency for (2) was 128 ms. Although the latency requirement was not satisfied, our analysis indicates that it can be reduced by dividing satellites into more subgroups and equipping each satellite with additional mmWave modules.

title: Research and Development of Sewerage Infrastructure Sensing System Using Unlicensed Band Multi-hop LPWA.
abstract: Due to global warming, sudden urban disasters, such as urban flooding caused by localized heavy rainfall and large-scale sinkholes due to aging sewer infrastructure, are becoming a major problem. Regarding inland flooding in particular, there are already examples of initiatives to predict inland flooding through simulations based on inland flood analysis models. However, there are many cases of unexpected disasters that are difficult to predict through simulation alone, such as unidentified water. Therefore, in addition to simulations, it is becoming more effective to monitor the condition of the sewer system below the manhole in real time on the ground using various sensing data such as water level sensors, water flow sensors, and environmental sensors. Because steel manhole covers are generally disadvantageous from a wireless communication perspective, there are several examples of sensing initiatives using mobile networks and cellular systems (licensed bands) LPWA with high signal strength. In this study, we have realized a flexible and scalable multi-hop WSN communication system that can monitor sewerage infrastructure using unlicensed LPWA, without using mobile networks or cellular LPWA. The system utilizes a multi-hop WSN of unlicensed band LPWA to receive weakened radio signals transmitted through the manhole cover at a repeater above the manhole, and then transmits them via multi-hop to a remote location. The system's effectiveness was confirmed through a demonstration experiment using an actual manhole site. We will continue to build a platform that aims to enable multimodal sensing of real-time water level sensing data, open weather data, and video data of the ground around the manhole.
